definitions.gloss: to be utterly exhausted; to be completely worn out
definitions.explanation: To be exhausted to the absolute limit, both physically and mentally. The 果てる suffix intensifies 疲れる to mean total, complete exhaustion.

examples.japanese: {一日中|いちにちじゅう}{歩|ある}いて{疲|つか}れ{果|は}てた。
examples.english: I walked all day and was completely exhausted.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れ{果|は}てて、{家|いえ}に{着|つ}いたらすぐ{寝|ね}てしまった。
examples.english: I was so exhausted that I fell asleep as soon as I got home.

examples.japanese: {長時間|ちょうじかん}の{会議|かいぎ}と{残業|ざんぎょう}が{続|つづ}き、{心身|しんしん}ともに{疲|つか}れ{果|は}てていた。
examples.english: After long meetings and overtime one after another, I was completely exhausted both physically and mentally.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Compound verb: {疲|つか}れる (to get tired) + {果|は}てる (to reach the end). The {果|は}てる suffix is a common intensifier meaning "to do something to completion" or "to the very end." Other examples: {使|つか}い{果|は}たす (use up completely), {朽|く}ち{果|は}てる (decay completely).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {疲|つか}れ{果|は}てた{顔|かお} (an utterly exhausted face)
- {疲|つか}れ{果|は}てた{体|からだ} (a completely worn-out body)
- {心身|しんしん}ともに{疲|つか}れ{果|は}てる (be exhausted both physically and mentally)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {疲|つか}れる: to get tired — basic form, milder degree
- くたくたになる: to be worn out — colloquial, vivid expression
- {消耗|しょうもう}する: to be depleted — more formal, can apply to resources as well as energy
